organism.scientificName: Chlamydia trachomatis serovar D (strain ATCC VR-885 / DSM 19411 / UW-3/Cx)

fullName.value: Chlamydia protein associating with death domains

texts.value: Involved in de novo para-aminobenzoate (PABA) biosynthesis (PubMed:23972426, PubMed:32967910, PubMed:36122239, PubMed:36647787, PubMed:37936269). Acts as a self-sacrificing or 'suicide' enzyme that utilizes its own active site tyrosine residue as the substrate for PABA synthesis (PubMed:32967910, PubMed:36122239, PubMed:36647787, PubMed:37936269). The side chain of the tyrosine residue is released from the protein backbone via cleavage of the C(alpha)-C(beta) bond, leaving a glycine in place of the original tyrosine residue (PubMed:32967910, PubMed:36122239, PubMed:36647787, PubMed:37936269). Additionally, a lysine is deaminated and oxidized to aminoadipic acid, acting as a sacrificial amino group donor (PubMed:36647787, PubMed:37936269). Reaction requires O(2) and a reduced dimetal cofactor (PubMed:32967910, PubMed:36122239, PubMed:36647787, PubMed:37936269). Ascorbate can be used as electron donor in vitro (PubMed:36122239, PubMed:37936269)

Was also identified as a specific toxin that associates with death domains of tumor necrosis factor family (TNF) receptors and induces apoptosis in mammalian cell lines through a Caspase-dependent mechanism

reaction.name: L-tyrosyl-[protein] + L-ascorbate + L-lysyl-[protein] + 2 O2 = glycyl-[protein] + (S)-2-amino-6-oxohexanoyl-[protein] + 4-aminobenzoate + L-dehydroascorbate + 2 H2O + 2 H(+)

texts.value: Binds 2 divalent metal cations per subunit (PubMed:15087448). Can use a diiron cofactor for catalysis (PubMed:32967910, PubMed:36647787). However, activity is much higher in vitro in the presence of manganese, or in the presence of both iron and manganese (PubMed:36122239, PubMed:36647787). The physiological cofactor is most likely a heterodinuclear Mn(2+)/Fe(2+) cluster (PubMed:36122239, PubMed:36647787, PubMed:37936269, PubMed:39471288).

The protein is a cosubstrate rather than a true enzyme and is left in an inactive state after a single turnover (PubMed:32967910, PubMed:36122239, PubMed:36647787, PubMed:37936269). Inactive under anaerobic conditions (PubMed:32967910)

Homodimer (PubMed:15087448, PubMed:39471288). During infection, interacts with death domains of mammalian tumor necrosis factor (TNF) family receptors Fas, DR4, DR5 and to some extent TNFR1, but not with the respective downstream adapters (PubMed:11805081)
Secreted into the host cytoplasm, where it co-localizes with Fas in the proximity of the inclusion body
In infected epithelial cells, is expressed late in the infectious cycle
Can complement the PABA-auxotrophic E.coli mutant lacking pabA, pabB and pabC genes
